issue.title: Supervisor-owned procs and the sase shell model
issue.description: Every durable proc is detached and supervisor-owned, monitors are a proc-shell facade, ACE owns no proc execution, and SASE presents one coherent agent-and-shell taxonomy.

issue.title: Sase agent and shell taxonomy
issue.description: shell-taxonomy: plan and land the behavior-preserving terminology migration, glossary model, compatibility aliases, CLI language, and generated memory surfaces.

issue.title: Unified proc-shell platform
issue.description: proc-shell-platform: plan and land the Rust-backed proc schema, atomic lifecycle, hardened detached supervisor, named proc shells, family attachment, and monitor service facade.

issue.title: Supervisor ownership for every ACE proc
issue.description: ace-proc-ownership: plan and land durable command/result migrations for ACE proc producers, global concurrency enforcement, read-only observation, and detached-option retirement.

payload.entry: Closed after child epic sase-m9.2.1 completed and was closed without force. Phase outcome is landed on master: Rust-backed atomic proc lifecycle, detached supervisor ownership, named proc-shell CLI, family-attached monitor facade, and compatibility cutover are complete. Its independent follow-up/test-gate debt remains tracked on dedicated task beads and does not block the parent phase.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: Proposed by phase sase-mc.5.2 and reproduced by land agent on current master 3b810036f: sase monitor show g6g21192dysz --all-lines crashes in list_monitors with ValueError because ace-run artifact 20260815145837 has agent_family_role=monitor but no monitor_id. This is unrelated to provider disabling and causally belongs to the active supervisor-owned proc/monitor-facade epic; monitor listing/show must tolerate or correctly classify legacy/malformed monitor-role artifacts.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: Independently reproduced while finishing task sase-me on current master 5b4d5b3c6: sase monitor show vhy8mhvgd48q --all-lines crashes in list_monitors with ValueError because ace-run artifact 20260815145837 is not a monitor member. This blocks retained-log inspection for a completed monitor and corroborates the existing malformed monitor-role artifact report; causal owner is the active supervisor-owned proc/monitor-facade epic.

Child epic sase-m9.3.1 closeout is blocked: monitored just check-full xbfsm7s2nb5e failed (11 failed / 30981 passed). Failures classified as unrelated standing flakes (sase-mv/sase-j7 config-cache cascade, sase-n5 Models panel, sase-n6 fakey timeout) plus a start-ack timing DISCOVERED ISSUE on sase-m9.3.1. sase-ml / sase-m9.3.1 / sase-m9.3 were not closed. Evidence: file:explicit:c336e6b753af7be80078a3ea.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: monitor lane helpers do one full proc-store read per candidate record. src/sase/monitor/store.py:143 active_monitor_for_lane and :165 monitor_blocking_start_for_lane both loop over _monitor_records(project_name) and call should_reconcile_dead_supervisor(monitor) per candidate with no shared snapshot, so each candidate re-reads and re-parses the whole proc store. This became expensive when sase-m9.2.1.4 (8b4635ad1 'feat(monitor): run monitors through the shared proc service') put proc_shell_owns() -- a full proc-store read via get_proc() -- inside that guard. Callers are CLI start/inspect paths: src/sase/monitor/start.py:322 and src/sase/main/monitor_handler.py:399, not the TUI list. The fix primitive already exists: epic sase-n7 added sase.procs.store.read_proc_snapshot() plus snapshot= kwargs on get_proc(), proc_shell_owns(), should_reconcile_dead_supervisor(), and reconcile_dead_supervisor(); the lane helpers just need to read one snapshot per pass and thread it through, exactly as reconcile_dead_supervisors_for_records() and list_monitors() now do. Measured shape on the author's real state before sase-n7: 147 monitor records x ~101 procs = 14,847 Proc.from_dict calls per pass. Proposed by bead sase-n7.2 and routed here by sase-n7.land because sase-m9 introduced the expensive guard.

LANDED epic sase-m9 (Supervisor-owned procs and the sase shell model).

VERIFIED (step 1). Read all three phases, both closed child epics and their phases, and every note in the tree (sase-m9.1/.1.1/.1.1.1-.3, sase-m9.2/.2.1/.2.1.1-.6 incl. repair epic .6.1-.3, sase-m9.3/.3.1/.3.1.1-.5), then checked the source and the epic's commits rather than the reports. Taxonomy (4280bc990, e923dcb5d, 2265f2618, 76356cf57): SaseAgentRef lives at src/sase/sase_agent.py:38, glossary carries Sase Agent/Sase Shell/Proc Shell/Agent Shell, and grep finds no 'agent lane' left in src/, docs/, or sase/memory/. Proc-shell platform (152268b59, 11072ba5d, 1e242aa8b, 8b4635ad1, ca93686a6, ffce3c842, 4ba7ee812): 'sase proc run -N/--shell' addresses named shells and the sase-core-rs floor sits at the published proc-lifecycle release. ACE ownership (07e254a42, 0835b38d2, 7d7581a21, 8c4840458, ac5d95810): src/sase/ops/ holds the durable operation contracts, ProcObserver is a read-only daemon-thread projection, 'sase proc run' has no -d/--detached, and the retired token still emits its suppressed diagnostic. The two AST conformance gates that keep this true - tests/test_proc_submission_static_invariants.py and tests/ace/tui/test_proc_producer_inventory.py - both pass, so no post-epic commit reintroduced a callable producer or a legacy proc kind. 215 monitor/proc/ops/observer tests pass on master a892dce3a.

Epic-bead notes resolved. The two 'sase monitor show ... --all-lines' ValueError reports (sase-mc.5.land, sase-me--1) are fixed by e38874024; re-ran 'sase monitor show' for g6g21192dysz, vhy8mhvgd48q and 2v69a1dn60aa on the host store - all exit 0. The sase-n7.land N+1 report is fixed by this landing (below).

INTEGRATED (step 2). Reviewed the 153 non-epic commits since 2026-08-14 19:16 EDT for code that should now use, duplicate, or conflict with what this epic added. One real gap, exactly as routed to this epic by sase-n7.land: epic sase-n7 added sase.procs.store.read_proc_snapshot() plus snapshot= kwargs and threaded them through reconcile_dead_supervisors_for_records() and list_monitors(), but the monitor lane helpers were left behind while sase-m9.2.1.4 (8b4635ad1) had put proc_shell_owns() - a full proc-store read - inside their per-candidate guard. Fixed as ccbcb3557: active_monitor_for_lane and monitor_blocking_start_for_lane now share one lazily-read ProcStoreSnapshot per scan, so a scan does one store read instead of one per candidate and a lane with no monitor member does none. Regression tests fail against the old ordering (8 reads vs 1). The same commit thread-scopes the shared proc-store read counter in tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py, because sase-n7.4 (39bdd6772) moved reconciliation onto asyncio.to_thread and a background pass could otherwise inflate those counters (the class filed as task sase-nj). Reviewed and found already integrated, not conflicting: 2a587fff7 (phantom running procs) builds on this epic's observer/projection model; 6d9db4c26 / 3f3f61d14 / 9fe82045d / 39bdd6772 are sase-n7 perf work on the same guard; 1d83e7a64 (Agent Lane -> Agent Node) extends this epic's taxonomy consistently. Verification: fmt, ruff, mypy, keep-sorted, feature-flag schema, pyscripts, test-waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology, toobig, SASE validation and committed-plan validation all pass; test-scoped ran 1489 passed / 1 failed / 3 skipped.

FOLLOW-UP DISPOSITIONS. Fixed in-epic: sase-core-rs proc-lifecycle floor (4ba7ee812); settlement crash recovery (ca93686a6, ffce3c842); stale sase-m9.3.1.2 Symvision entry and the inventory-test formatting break; SASE_PROC_* test hermeticity, malformed monitor-row enumeration, and session-worker projection (e38874024, with task sase-ml closed on that evidence); the start-ack supervisor-pid contract (71061cead); the lane-helper N+1 (ccbcb3557). Routed to task beads: sase-m7 (+1, FORCE_COLOR/ANSI substring assertions), sase-ma (Models effort-picker PNG drift), sase-ll (in-agent 'sase monitor start' misparsing '.N' phase-worker names), sase-j0 (test-cost/flake-baseline gate debt), sase-ng (retire the dead in-process launch/cleanup bodies and the vestigial proc_callable parameter), sase-ne (reconcile's locked settle path still runs a full-history index query per candidate via get_monitor - deliberately left out of ccbcb3557, which changes only the proc-store read and leaves the injected get_monitor callable untouched). Routed to other active epics: the Artifacts/Beads select_entry_target visual failure to sase-m6. Not epic-attributable and left with their owners: the 03a session-worker-visibility note is superseded by the e38874024 overlay, and the 03a 'no agent artifacts found' monitor-start report was resolved by the successful in-agent monitor z2awr5avszsa. Declined to create anything new for the two standing full-lane flake classes (sase-mv/sase-j7, sase-n5, sase-n6) - all already have ready beads.
